title: A penalty set with sector 37 reduces Fourier errors across 6 to 12 minute gaps in two TESS sectors of TIC 300651846
abstract: We test a smoothness penalty for Fourier profile fits of the known complex periodic variable TIC 300651846. We choose the penalty on TESS sector 37, then fix it for sectors 32 and 64. The penalty reduces large prediction errors across 6 to 12 minute sample gaps. It does not give stable evidence that a changing profile predicts better than a shifted and scaled rigid profile. Controls retain time correlation by circular shifts of observed residuals. They are sensitivity tests, not a pure instrumental null. This is a stronger method check on existing observations, not a new source or planet. The finite penalty grid, selected test sectors, phase holes, residual controls and lack of independent telescope data limit physical claims. Code, all cycle losses, aggregate results, figures and exact input hashes are included. External observations remain outside the publication.

display.caption: Free-profile prediction gain relative to a shifted and scaled template, with and without the fixed smoothness penalty. Crosses give median residual controls at the longest gap. Sectors 32 and 64 are repeat observations of one star. They are not independent telescope confirmation.
